findings.evidence:
`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1511`–`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1523`: in `HashGroupKey` (decimal path), on `EncodeDecimal` error it immediately `return buf, err` (same pattern for time at `pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1524`–`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1536`).
`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go:149`–`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go:157`: `GetGroupKey` runs `err = errCtx.HandleError(err)` and continues when the error is downgraded to warning/ignored.
`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_partial_worker.go:224`–`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_partial_worker.go:253`: HashAgg uses `groupKey[i]` bytes directly as hash/map keys (`murmur3.Sum32(groupKey[i])` and `mapper[...][string(groupKey[i])]`). Any rows left with empty/missing key bytes will be grouped/deduped incorrectly.
`pkg/util/codec/decimal.go:25`–`pkg/util/codec/decimal.go:34`: `EncodeDecimal` clamps `frac > mysql.MaxDecimalScale` to 30, then calls `dec.WriteBin(...)` which can return `types.ErrTruncated`.
`pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:274`–`pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:285` + `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:84`–`pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:108`: `AVG(DECIMAL)` can produce `retTp.decimal = old.decimal + div_precision_increment` (>30) and final result is rounded to that `frac`, so `MyDecimal` can have `digitsFrac > 30`.
The added test demonstrates this path is reachable and warning is surfaced: `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/aggregate.result:2062`–`tests/integrationtest/r/executor/aggregate.result:2066` shows warning 1265 with raw `%s/%d` placeholders (consistent with returning `types.ErrTruncated` without args from decimal encoding).
findings.fix:
In `HashGroupKey`, avoid returning early on per-row encode errors that can be downgraded by `ErrCtx`.
- Continue encoding remaining rows, while recording the first (or aggregated) error to return after finishing the loop.
- For the time path, avoid overwriting `buf[i]` with `nil` if `EncodeMySQLTime` returns `nil, err` (use a temporary and keep the pre-existing slice content).
- Consider switching decimal group-key encoding to a lossless representation for `digitsFrac > 30` (e.g. `MyDecimal.ToHashKey()`/string-based encoding) to avoid truncation collisions, instead of clamping to 30.
findings.impact: Silent wrong results risk when `EncodeDecimal`/`EncodeMySQLTime` errors are treated as warnings/ignored: `HashGroupKey` may return a partially-filled `groupKey` where rows after the first error keep empty/missing key bytes. HashAgg will then merge unrelated rows into the same group (or drop distinct values), corrupting `GROUP BY` / `SELECT DISTINCT` / hash-agg semantics for multi-row chunks.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `git show upstream/master:pkg/util/codec/codec.go` still returns early on encode error (`return buf, err`) in `HashGroupKey`. File history after this commit only includes unrelated changes (`6e98fdeda5` string/collator optimization; `96bdeae43c` join key prealloc), and `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go` remains unchanged in this aspect.
findings.verify: Add an integration test that exercises multi-row hashing with a warning-producing decimal key, e.g. a query that produces multiple rows of `AVG(DECIMAL(65,30))` (so output scale >30) and applies `SELECT DISTINCT` over them, asserting all distinct rows are preserved. Also add a unit test for `HashGroupKey` ensuring it updates every `buf[i]` even when `EncodeDecimal` returns `types.ErrTruncated`.
findings.what: `HashGroupKey` now returns non-nil `buf` on decimal/time encode error (to survive when the error is downgraded), but it still returns immediately on the *first* row error. Because `GetGroupKey` may downgrade truncation errors to warnings/ignored via `ErrCtx`, HashAgg can proceed with a partially-filled `groupKey` (rows after the first error remain empty/missing suffix), leading to incorrect grouping/deduplication for chunks with more than one row.

subject: codec: should also return the value even with error because the error may be ignored in the future (#62175)
summary: Commit changes `codec.HashGroupKey` to return `buf` (not `nil`) on `EncodeDecimal`/`EncodeMySQLTime` errors and updates tests for issue #61735. This prevents panics when truncation errors are downgraded to warnings, but because `HashGroupKey` still exits on the first row error and HashAgg uses `groupKey` bytes directly as the map key, warning/ignored errors can yield partially/empty keys for later rows and produce wrong `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT` results. No later fix found up to `upstream/master`.
